numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Casting a datetime64/timedelta64 SparseArray to an integer or boolean Sparse dtype resolves the target fill_value to the subtype default (0/False) instead of converting the source fill_value, so every unstored position densifies to the wrong value. For the PR example the sparse cast gives [0, 0, 1451779200000000000] instead of the dense cast's first two values.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: The source datetimelike fill_value should be converted to the target subtype, so unstored positions densify to the same integers as the dense cast, e.g. [1451692800000000000, 1451692800000000000, 1451779200000000000].
trigger_conditions: SparseArray with datetime64 or timedelta64 subtype
cast to an integer or boolean Sparse dtype (e.g. Sparse[int64])
fill_value is a datetimelike value such as pd.Timestamp, pd.Timedelta, pd.NaT, or a unit-less np.datetime64('NaT')
fully dense arrays (npoints == len) must also convert the fill_value, which the earlier code skipped
an explicitly non-default target fill_value must be respected rather than replaced by the subtype default
